newsitem.title: INDONESIA: FORECAST - Indonesia Telkom future clouded.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Indonesia Telkom future clouded.

text.p: PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia (Telkom) said on Thursday it posted a sharp rise in its 1996 net profit, but uncertainty over a possible competitor linked to President Suharto is clouding its outlook, analysts said.
Telkom posted a net profit of 1.5 trillion rupiah in 1996 against 906.9 billion rupiah in 1995.
Frederic Thomas, an analyst with brokerage firm PT Peregrine Sewu Securities, said the market consensus was that Telkom would post a net profit of around 1.4 trillion rupiah in 1996.
"The 1996 net profit was above market consensus and also above our expectations," Thomas said, adding his prediction was slightly below the market consensus figure. He declined to give details.
"Will Telkom be able to maintain the strong growth? That's interesting to know because of the uncertainties over the new competitor," Thomas said.
Reports in local newspapers on Monday named the possible rival as the Jakarta Tower consortium, whose members include President Suharto's brother-in-law businessman Sudwikatmono.
The reports said it could end Telkom's monopoly in basic telecommunications services which included domestic short and long distance calls. The reports mentioned no firm dates.
However, in afternoon conference call with analysts on Thursday, Telkom's President Director Asman Akhir Nasution said the new firm's services would not include telephone calls.

Despite Nasution's comment another foreign analyst, who declined to be named, said due to past expereince with the often fluid Indonesian business climate, investors were likely to demand a discount due to the uncertainty.

"Unlike other cases, Telkom is listed not just here but overseas as well. So it would not be that easy to change the regulations as it would have negative impacts on Indonesian privatation programe," the foreign analyst said.
According the government regulations, Telkom has the exclusive rights to provide local call services until the year 2010 for short distance calls and 2005 for long distance calls.

Indonesia allowed PT Satelindo, set up in 1993 and controlled by President Suharto's son Bambang Trihatmodjo, to end state-owned PT Indonesia Satelit Corp's (Indosat) monopoly in international telephone services.
The government's permit was given before Indosat listed its shares in October 1994, the analyst said.
Agung Prabowo, a telecommunications analyst with the large state-owned brokerage firm PT Danareksa, however, said investors should have not be so wary about the possible competitor.

"They should have known that the monopoly should not be interpreted as absolute monopoly. It's mentioned in Telkom's prospectus that competition is allowed as long as it has a link-up with Telkom," Prabowo said.
Telkom said on Thursday it had signed an agreement late last week with the consortium to provide only multimedia services such as video-on-demand.
Telkom fell 25 rupiah to close at 3,725 rupiah in active trading on Thursday.
